skill.name: config-auditing
skill.description: Guides Neovim configuration audits with checklists, deprecated API checks, best practices, and structured report templates.
skill.summary: Audit Neovim configurations for deprecated APIs, security risks, structure issues, and performance problems.
skill.author: BitYoungjae

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation examples that inspect the standard Neovim configuration directory, not hidden malware behavior. I confirmed one secret-disclosure risk because the checklist can print full hardcoded credentials, and I added a semantic finding for headless Neovim commands that execute user configuration.

remediation.issue: Headless Neovim commands execute user configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for explicit confirmation, prefer static file inspection first, and use --clean or -u NONE when version checks do not require user config.

remediation.issue: Secret scanning can reveal full credential values.
remediation.suggestion: Redact matched values before reporting, and show only file path, line number, key name, and rotation guidance.

remediation.issue: Audit commands assume standard home paths.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve config paths with Neovim stdpath or XDG variables, and explain what directories will be read.

remediation.issue: Startup profiling uses a fixed temporary log path.
remediation.suggestion: Use a unique temporary path and remove the log after profiling.

semantic_findings.title: Headless Neovim Commands Execute User Configuration
semantic_findings.description: The skill asks agents to run headless Neovim commands and explicitly load the user's init.lua. This can execute local configuration or plugin startup code during an audit.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited commands invoke Neovim without --clean, and line 44 calls dofile on the user's init.lua. That is direct execution of local configuration code.

content.value_statement: Neovim configurations can accumulate deprecated APIs, slow startup paths, and unsafe patterns. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured checks and clear fixes.
actual_capabilities: Runs or suggests checks for Neovim version, config path, Lua file counts, plugins, startup time, and startup errors.
Reviews config structure for monolithic files, plugin manager leftovers, hardcoded paths, and duplicate settings.
Flags deprecated Neovim APIs by version and points to modern replacements.
Checks lazy.nvim patterns, plugin loading choices, keymaps, options, and performance anti-patterns.
Searches Neovim Lua files for hardcoded secret-like assignments.
Produces a graded audit report with critical issues, warnings, suggestions, statistics, and fixes.
limitations: Requires permission to inspect local Neovim configuration files before accurate results are possible.
Shell commands can execute the user's Neovim configuration unless the operator chooses safer static inspection.
It does not replace a full malware review of installed plugins or remote plugin sources.
Deprecated API guidance can lag behind future Neovim releases and should be checked against current release notes.

use_cases.title: Personal Config Health Check
use_cases.description: Review one Neovim setup for startup issues, deprecated APIs, risky settings, and cleanup opportunities.

use_cases.title: Team Dotfiles Review
use_cases.description: Apply a consistent checklist before sharing team dotfiles or onboarding developers to a common editor setup.

use_cases.title: Migration Readiness Audit
use_cases.description: Find packer.nvim leftovers, removed APIs, and lazy.nvim changes before a Neovim version upgrade.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Health Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner audit for a local setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my Neovim configuration at the standard config path. Ask before running commands that execute my config. Summarize critical issues first.

prompt_templates.title: Deprecated API Scan
prompt_templates.scenario: Compatibility review for a known Neovim version
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my Neovim version and scan my Lua config for APIs deprecated or removed for that version. Provide replacements.

prompt_templates.title: Performance Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review startup performance, plugin loading, autocmds, and keymaps. Separate measured findings from suggestions.

prompt_templates.title: Full Security and Compatibility Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a complete audit using the checklist, best practices, and deprecated API guide. Redact any secret values before reporting results.

output_examples.input: Audit my current Neovim config for deprecated APIs.
output: Summary: Neovim compatibility issues were found in two Lua files.
Priority: replace deprecated buffer option APIs before upgrading.
Next step: review the listed files and apply the documented modern alternatives.

output_examples.input: Review startup performance and plugin loading.
output: Summary: startup load count is high, and several plugins load before they are needed.
Recommendation: move filetype tools to filetype triggers and defer user interface extras.
Evidence: the report separates measured startup data from style suggestions.

output_examples.input: Check for security issues in my Neovim config.
output: Summary: one secret-like assignment pattern was detected and the value was redacted.
Action: move the value to an environment variable and rotate it if it was committed.
Safety note: commands that execute user config should require confirmation.

best_practices: Ask for approval before running headless Neovim commands that load user configuration.
Redact secret values and report only file paths, variable names, and remediation steps.
Run version checks before applying deprecated API guidance.
anti_patterns: Do not paste complete token, password, or API key matches into the final audit.
Do not treat every grep match as a defect without reading nearby context.
Do not run plugin update or install commands during an audit unless explicitly requested.

faq.question: What does this skill audit?
faq.answer: It audits Neovim configuration structure, deprecated APIs, lazy.nvim patterns, performance risks, keymaps, options, and security-sensitive settings.

faq.question: Does it change my Neovim files?
faq.answer: No. The skill is a review guide. File changes should only happen after a separate explicit request.

faq.question: Why does it need shell access?
faq.answer: Some checks use local commands to measure startup time, inspect config files, and detect deprecated API usage.

faq.question: Can it expose secrets?
faq.answer: Yes, secret scanning can match real values. Results should redact values and show only safe evidence.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: How should I use it safely?
faq.answer: Start with static file inspection, approve any command execution, and redact sensitive values before sharing results.
